frames.caption: Everything in this demo runs from one FirstBank workspace: the customer’s app, the branch desk, operations, the core banking and messaging views, and the control tower.
Olumuyiwa Dada walks into FirstBank’s Alapere branch with the account-opening form he has already filled in by hand. This is the relationship manager’s desk.
Open an account: every application the branch is working on, and where each one is in its case.
A new application.
Instead of typing the paper form in, they upload a scan of it.
The form is read page by page, in the browser. (Identifiers on this sample scan are blacked out for the demo.)
Every field read off the form, each with how sure the read is. A low score marks a field to check, not a guess passed off as fact.
They take the details into the application.

frames.title: Checked with him, step by step, and submitted

frames.caption: The application has filled itself in from the form. The relationship manager checks each step with Olumuyiwa instead of retyping it.
frames.short: The application fills itself in from the form; each step is checked with the customer.

frames.caption: Name and contact details are right. On to identity…
…his BVN and NIN, as written on the form…
…his address…
…his work…
…and the account he wants, with his next of kin.
One last look at everything before it goes in.
Olumuyiwa confirms the details are his and consents to FirstBank verifying them with NIBSS, NIMC and its screening partners.
Submit. That starts his account-opening case in UiPath Maestro.
Received, with a reference. The checks start in the background straight away.

frames.title: KYC with him at the desk: the face check

frames.caption: He is still at the desk, so instead of sending him a link the relationship manager completes KYC with him now.

frames.url: recorded: FaceID on Microsoft Azure · UiBank demo tenant
frames.caption: His documents, then the face check — recorded here on the live Microsoft Azure service: Azure confirms a live person and matches the face to the identity on file. In the Verify console: the selfie against the passport on file (blurred), face match and liveness pass, the anti-spoof checks and the audit record.
frames.short: Documents, then a live face check on Microsoft Azure: liveness and face match pass.

frames.caption: He signs with his finger, and KYC is complete: documents, liveness, face match and signature, all on his record.
On the pipeline, his application is already live in UiPath Maestro, at Intake.
Open it.
The next best action leads: the case has done its own intake work — read the form, looked him up, pulled his existing relationships — and is waiting on a person for the duplicate and risk pre-screen.
frames.short: The next best action: the case is waiting on a person at Intake.

frames.caption: The live case: five stages, and every step of the current one with its status. Only the gate needs a person.
Olumuyiwa already banks with FirstBank and nothing is on the risk list, so the relationship manager approves. The case moves to Verification.
Verification ran on its own: NIN with NIMC, BVN with NIBSS, AML, PEP and fraud screening, all clear. Each one can be opened.

Screening found a close match for his name on a watchlist. Instead of parking the case for a person, Maestro hands it to the voice agent — an AI agent that rings Olumuyiwa now to confirm his date and place of birth.
frames.short: A name match on a watchlist: the voice agent rings Olumuyiwa to confirm who he is.

frames.caption: In the case, Voice Agent opens as its own stage beside Verification: place the call, speak to the customer, end the call, update the next steps.
He confirms, so the match is not him. The call ends, it is logged on the case, and the case returns to Verification on its own — no one at the bank had to pick up the phone.

frames.url: recorded: Voice agent on Azure Voice Live · UiBank demo tenant
frames.caption: Recorded on the live service: the desk turns red while the voice agent is on the call, and in Maestro the Voice Agent stage runs its steps — place the call, speak to the customer, end the call, update the next steps.
frames.short: Recorded live: the desk shows the call, and Maestro runs the Voice Agent stage.

frames.url: recorded: Voice agent on Azure Voice Live · UiBank demo tenant
frames.caption: The relationship manager can place a call too. Here the case is waiting on missing documents, so the next best action is to call him: the voice agent introduces itself, confirms it is speaking to Olumuyiwa and checks his date of birth — with a live transcript as it talks.
frames.short: The RM places a call: the agent verifies him, with a live transcript.

frames.caption: The NIN check…
…is the real NIMC call: what was sent, what came back, how long it took, and each field matched against the application. It can be re-run from here.
The BVN check with NIBSS, the same way.
Document checks…
…judged against the bank’s Document rules: each check, its outcome and the rule row that decided it. A referral asks a person; nothing is silently blocked.
Back to the case.
No exceptions to review, so the analyst gate is approved…
…the routing rules found nothing that needs enhanced due diligence, and the officer approves the decision.
Activation ran: FirstBank’s core banking has opened his CIF and account 8106921974, set up his channels and card, and told him.
Activation is signed off…
…and Closure assembles the case packet and the audit report.
Done: every stage complete in Maestro, the account fully active, and every step on the record.
frames.short: The case is complete and the account fully active.

frames.title: Finacle, the event stream and the customer

frames.caption: In Finacle, the core banking system: Olumuyiwa’s CIF and account 8106921974, active.
On the event stream, every step of his case as it happened — the application, the checks, the account, the notifications — for any other system to act on.
And the messages he received: the welcome, with his new account number.
Behind the desk is UiPath Maestro case management. This is a live onboarding case on the tenant: the case plan the desk has been reading all along — and, below, its execution trail.
frames.short: The case in UiPath Maestro: the case plan and its execution trail.

frames.caption: The plan in full…

Five primary stages — Intake, Verification, Decision, Activation, Closure — each with its tasks: robots and agents run in parallel, a person only at the gate (marked *). Entry points on the left: branch tablet, mobile app, fax, email, a regulatory deadline.
Below, the secondary stages the case can divert into and come back from: EDD review for high-risk and PEP cases, compliance escalations, pending customer, and the terminal declined / withdrawn.
Green is done, with how long each stage took. This case is at Decision, waiting on the onboarding officer — and past its SLA, which is why it shows red.
frames.short: This case is at Decision, waiting on the officer and past its SLA.

frames.caption: The execution trail…

…every step the case took, in which stage and when: the trigger, the case manager — the AI orchestrator deciding what runs next — and each task. Beside it, the case variables; Action history and Incidents record every pause, cancel, reassignment and failure.
ABA Integrated Solutions Ltd, an IT company in Abuja, wants a corporate current account. Its director brings the completed corporate account-opening form to the branch.
A new application…
…for a company.
The completed corporate form is uploaded, all 13 pages.

Read the same way: the entity, its registration and tax numbers, the turnover, and the authorised officer who is director, signatory and beneficial owner. (Identifiers on this sample scan are blacked out.)
Into the application.

frames.title: The company and its director, checked and submitted

frames.caption: The company, exactly as registered — filled in from the form.
Its director and signatory, Adelaja Babajide Adetayo. Everyone who signs is verified with NIBSS in the background; more can be added.
A last check…
The signatory confirms the details and consents to the checks on the company and each director.
Submitted: the company’s own corporate onboarding case starts in Maestro.

frames.title: A corporate case, its own stages

frames.caption: On the pipeline beside Olumuyiwa’s, the company’s application, live at Intake.

The corporate case plan does more at Intake: it analyses the CAC pack, verifies the RC number with the CAC registry and the TIN with FIRS, then asks a person for the entity duplicate and risk pre-screen.
Clean, so it is approved.
The checks are open to inspect, as for an individual…
…with a tab for the directors.
Each director and signatory with their role and BVN — the people Verification checks, along with the beneficial owners.
Directors and beneficial owners verified, SCUML checked: approved…
…the corporate risk rating needs no enhanced due diligence, and the mandate decision is approved.
Activation: the corporate CIF and account 2801315367 in Finacle, the mandate and signing limits, the specimen signatures and online banking tokens.
The signatories are activated…
…and the corporate case closes with its packet and audit report.
ABA Integrated Solutions is open for business with FirstBank.
In Finacle, both new customers: the company’s account 2801315367 above Olumuyiwa’s.

frames.title: Twenty staff accounts in one upload

frames.caption: An employer is opening salary accounts for its staff. The relationship manager does not capture them one by one…
…it is a bulk upload.
Two channels into the same process: an Excel manifest of who may be onboarded, or a bundle of completed account-opening packages. This employer sends packages.
The batch is named…
frames.text: Lagos State Government — October staff drive

frames.caption: …as Employee Value Banking.
One ZIP: a folder per employee with their form, ID and utility bill. (Demo data — no real people.)
Nothing is created until intake has checked it.
Twenty customers found. Five go back with a reason instead of being silently dropped: no ID, a bill too old, no proof of address, a BVN that appears twice, and a file in no one’s folder.
frames.short: Intake checks every folder: 15 accepted, 5 returned with a reason.

frames.caption: The other fifteen are processed.
Each one is verified in parallel — NIN, BVN, TIN, ID, sanctions, watchlists, adverse media — and reconciled against the form. Here the first eight run as live Maestro cases.

frames.title: The maker confirms what was read

frames.caption: Now operations, as the maker.
The maker’s queue. The scanned forms were read by OCR, so a person confirms each one before any account exists — lowest confidence first.
The first one.
The form beside what was read from it. The date of birth was read at 69%, so it is ringed on both sides; the sources reconcile, and every check has already run.
Correct, so it is approved and the next one opens.
A second person — the verifier — authorises. Maker and checker are always different people.
Each account with its post-no-debit position set by rule: savings and salary accounts open operative; a current account opens on PND until its documents are complete.
Create the accounts. It is idempotent: a retry never opens a second account for the same application.
Back with the relationship manager…
…the batch: accounts open, the exceptions with their reasons, and nothing left unexplained.
frames.short: The batch: accounts open, every exception with its reason.

frames.title: My desk: what needs me next

frames.caption: The relationship manager’s day starts on My desk. One card says what to do next and why — here a bulk-batch application with a check only a person can clear.
Then the numbers that matter: what needs them, what is breaching its SLA, what is in flight with no action needed, and how much of their book went straight through.
Every application they own — walk-in, corporate and bulk — sorted by what needs them first, with its live Maestro stage.
Approvals: requests from across the branch that need their authority — payments, limits, waivers, exceptions — with the value and the SLA.
An overdraft limit increase for Meridian Trading…
…with the maker’s justification and the facts beside it. It is above the RM’s own limit, so the recommendation is to route it for dual approval. Every decision is logged with a reason code.
frames.short: Each request with its justification; above their limit it routes for dual approval.

frames.caption: Clients: their key relationships, each with a headline — a deposit maturing, churn risk, an overdraft near its limit, a dormant account, KYC due.
A premier client…

…with next best actions worked out from her accounts: a ₦250m term deposit matures in 7 days, so offer the rollover; she holds no investments despite high balances, so schedule a portfolio review. Her products, signals and notes sit beside them.
frames.short: Each client with next best actions, products, signals and notes.

frames.caption: The operations analyst works every application that did not go straight through — from every channel and branch — in one workbench.
Across the top: straight-through rate against its 80% target, cases past SLA, unassigned work, and the reviewer hours automation gave back this week.
frames.short: The numbers: straight-through, past SLA, unassigned, hours returned.

frames.caption: Above them, the one thing to know first: how many cases are past SLA, and how many share a single cause — here the NIMC gateway timing out. Clear the cause, not the cases.

On the left, every way to slice the work: by view (needs attention, all, mine, unassigned), by pipeline queue — NIN, BVN, liveness, documents, Finacle — and exceptions and bulk failures. Below, the live health of each upstream service: NIMC recovered at 14:31, NIBSS degraded.
frames.short: Views, pipeline queues, and the live health of NIMC, NIBSS, liveness and Finacle.

frames.title: Fix the cause, not the cases

frames.caption: Needs attention groups the open cases by root cause, each with one action for all of them — retry NIN on every case the outage caught, retry BVN, request a new selfie, resend a chaser — or review them one by one.
NIMC is healthy again, so they are retried together.
One click instead of opening each case by hand.
All cases, sortable by urgency, risk, age or name.
A name mismatch: Aisha Yusuf.

The case opens on the problem: the form says Yusuff, NIMC says Yusuf — the difference highlighted, everything else matching. Beside it, the agent trail, every check, the risk score and why, and the applicant.
frames.short: The problem side by side, the trail, the checks and the risk.

frames.caption: Accept the NIMC spelling: it writes back to her application and the case carries on. J/K moves between cases, A accepts, R re-runs, E escalates.

That decision has been made before. The console learns from how people decide: Ruth has accepted the NIMC spelling on every one of 47 name mismatches — six weeks, no reversal. A policy nobody has written down.
The evidence…
…every one of the 47, weakest match first, and where they sit. A rule at 0.91 covers all 47, and the open cases it would settle are listed; its condition is written out in full.
frames.short: All 47 decisions, the threshold and the condition, in full.

frames.caption: Move the threshold and the coverage updates — at 0.94 it would cover fewer past decisions, so it would still send some to a person.
Promote at 0.91: about four cases a day stop landing on someone’s desk. A single reversal later pauses it.
Bulk failures: a payroll file from a corporate portal.
Ashaka Cement’s 180 rows…
…168 accounts opened; 12 failed, all at the NIN check, all in the same 18 minutes the NIMC gateway was down. The failures can be downloaded, or retried — only the 12, never the 168 already live.
frames.short: 168 opened, 12 failed during the NIMC outage: retry only the 12.

frames.caption: Retry the twelve.
Rules: what decides without a person.
Each live rule in plain words, its condition, and what it has done: cases deflected, reviewer hours returned, reversals. Any of them can be paused.
Edit…

…and the same rules are a DMN decision table — the standard format UiPath Maestro’s business-rule tasks run: when the check and condition match, then the automated action. Download it, and the case runs the same decision.
frames.short: The same rules as a DMN decision table.

frames.caption: The Document rules…

…the decision table every document is judged against: the document, the check, the condition, the outcome and the reason, each tied to a BRD rule. The hit policy is Collect — every rule that matches fires, and the strictest outcome wins.
frames.short: The Document rules as a DMN table: every match fires, strictest wins.

frames.caption: Policy changes: utility bills must now be under 60 days old, not 90.
Edited in the table…
…and saved. It is live: every document on every application is judged against the new rule from now on — no release, no developer.
In View, the rule reads in plain words with its new threshold, marked as edited — and Reset puts the bank’s default back.
